body.statement: The frontier theorem is equivalent, up to fixed constants, to \[R_T(B)\asymp\begin{cases}b^{-\alpha},&\alpha<1,\\ b^{-1}+T^{-1}\log(1+b),&\alpha=1,\\ b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1},&\alpha>1.\end{cases}\]
body.justification: The three regimes display when capacity, multiscale deadline accumulation, or the mandatory final pair determines regret.
body.gap: Adjacent papers report dimension-specific matching rates but do not derive this smoothness-by-dimension phase transition under a hard experimental reservoir.
body.consumer: The regime table converts a theorem into sample-size and memory guidance for trial planning.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(H_\alpha(b)=\sum_{r=1}^b r^{-\alpha}\).  If \(0<\alpha<1\), integral comparison gives constants depending only on \(\alpha\) such that
\[
c_\alpha b^{1-\alpha}\le H_\alpha(b)\le C_\alpha b^{1-\alpha}.
\]
Since \(b\le T/2\),
\[
T^{-1}H_\alpha(b)\le C_\alpha(b/T)b^{-\alpha}\le (C_\alpha/2)b^{-\alpha},
\]
while \(F_\alpha(T,b)\ge b^{-\alpha}\).  Thus \(F_\alpha(T,b)\asymp b^{-\alpha}\).  If \(\alpha=1\), integral comparison gives \(H_1(b)\asymp\log(1+b)\), so
\[
F_1(T,b)\asymp b^{-1}+T^{-1}\log(1+b).
\]
If \(\alpha>1\),
\[
1\le H_\alpha(b)\le1+\int_1^\infty x^{-\alpha}\,dx=1+(\alpha-1)^{-1},
\]
and hence \(F_\alpha(T,b)\asymp b^{-\alpha}+T^{-1}\).  Substitution into Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:minimax\text{-}frontier}\) yields the displayed three regimes.  Conversely, the same comparisons turn those three regime bounds back into bounds by fixed multiples of \(F_\alpha(T,b)\), proving the claimed equivalence.
